requirements.requirement: Route authentication and authorization messages on node1 to /var/log/auth-events.log.
requirements.summary: The authpriv selector targets /var/log/auth-events.log, rsyslog configuration validation succeeded, and live authpriv markers reached only the new file both before and after reboot.
Rsyslog remained active and enabled, while ordinary user.notice markers continued reaching /var/log/messages without entering the authentication log, including after reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence before and after reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged a scheduled reboot, changed boot identity, recovered rsyslog and persisted data, and successfully routed new authentication and normal-system events afterward.
limitations: The routing probes used synthetic logger messages with the authpriv and user facilities rather than an actual SSH, PAM, or sudo transaction, so producer-to-facility behavior was not independently sampled.
Commands cmd-27c3b4c95b3544de and cmd-31670e23dff6453e created rollback files under /var/tmp, but no final /var/tmp inventory confirms whether they remained.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated mutation was identified. Baseline and final marker writes were bounded evidence collection; the rsyslog and logrotate edits, service restart, and reboot directly supported implementation, validation, or the mandatory restart protocol. The restart protocol was complete and corroborated by fixed boot identities, with no final failed services, package inconsistency, or new exposure. Minor caveat: two rollback copies were created under /var/tmp and no later command shows their removal; because lifecycle inventory covered /tmp rather than /var/tmp, whether this task-related residue remained is unverified.
